summary: A first-person fiction excerpt in which the narrator meets Barry Morton, a senior official in Guatemala, and senses he is hiding something about what happened to a woman who is close to recovering her memory. Leaving, the narrator notices Morton's secretary wearing a jaguar-face silver pendant like ones seen earlier, though with a blank back, and wonders if she knows more. The narrator then turns to thoughts of Steve, whom they haven't seen in three and a half months.
one_line: In Guatemala, a narrator suspects official Barry Morton of hiding information and spots a jaguar pendant on his secretary resembling earlier clues.
key_facts: The narrator tells Barry Morton that a woman will soon remember what happened to her in Guatemala, hoping to provoke a reaction.
Barry Morton fiddles with an ornate letter opener with an onyx jaguar head on the handle.
Morton says the sovereign state of Guatemala 'definitely plays by its own rules'.
Morton says lower-level officials have a consensus that when foreigners meet with foul play, it is sometimes better not to be too industrious.
The narrator is certain Morton knows more than he is telling, though cannot say what feels wrong about him.
Morton's secretary is a stout, fiftyish Ladino matron with defiantly black-dyed hair and thick glasses with Zircon trim.
The secretary wears a small silver pendant shaped like a cat's face, most likely the local jaguar.
The pendant resembles ones the narrator remembers from Kevin and Rachel, but its back is blank silver with no engraving of lines and dots.
The narrator wonders whether the secretary handles things that never reach Morton's desk and may be the person to talk to.
The narrator has not seen Steve in three and a half months and feels that is about their limit.
The excerpt includes an unrelated sentence about Mandy seeing the original 'Garden of Earthly Delights' painting up close in 2013 after waiting in line for hours.
